(i) the string statistics problem can be solved in linear time, and (ii) a data structure that solves the statistics problem in linear time is available.

• the string statistics problem can be solved in linear time, • the maximum number of distinct non-overlappings of any substring along a given string can be retrieved in O ( w ) character comparisons, where w is the size of the query substring.

(a) the storage needed for the first kind of statistics is linear in the length n of x, and the retrieval is linear in the number of distinct substrings of x, (b) the storage needed in order to retrieve, in a number of comparisons not exceeding the period of w, the maximum number of distinct nonoverlapping instances of w along any x of length n is linear in n, and the retrieval of the maximum number of instances of w is linear in the period of w.
